input: # Generated by running the UPSTREAM reworkcss/css parser and keeping the
# rows this plugin already matched (see ../AGENTS.md, "Rules"). An expected
# value here is therefore never hand-written.
# That is why a rejection is a BARE `ERROR` and not `ERROR:<code>`. Upstream
# throws a CssSyntaxError; it has no tabnas error code to report, so a code
# in this file could only ever have been written by hand -- and pinning one
# here makes an external-conformance row fail when the engine changes WHICH
# code it raises, although upstream's requirement (reject this document) is
# still met. The codes themselves are pinned where they belong: this
# plugin's own contract, in comments.tsv and leniency.tsv.
thing { color: red; } /* b { color: blue; }
b { color: red; }\n{ color: green; }\na { color: blue; }
